attribution.note: Marcus's own testimony text on his Substack, stated in his own voice.

semantics.note: Retrospective observation from the May 2023 testimony to publication. The normalisation correctly ties 'nothing' to the independent review regime discussed in context.

contract.note: Reading 'did nothing' as the chamber not passing a mandatory pre-market review is an ordinary contextual reading, neither stretched for nor against him. A literal reading would be undercut by bills and hearings, so the interpretation matters.

evidence.note: Official record of Cruz's 9/29/2026 objection blocking UC passage of the AI Risk Management and Security Act. Consistent with the claim but covers only one attempt.
Contemporary reporting that Senate fast-track attempts failed and binding rules stalled. Corroborative, but not a full legislative history of the period.
Senator press release on a bill introduced in 2025. Under the contract, introduction does not count as chamber action, and it says nothing about disposition.

reviews.rationale: The evidence shows two failed passage attempts in September 2026 and reporting that federal legislation stalled. That fits the claim. But the contract requires records covering the whole May 2023 to Oct 2026 period, and it says failed action on selected bills cannot alone show no qualifying Senate action. The packet admits gaps: action histories were inaccessible and amendments and larger bills were not reviewed. Absence of passage is not established.
